title: Surgical degradation: bandwidth-aware KV eviction and deferred-retry adapter for GPU OOM prevention
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Under mixed workloads with long-context streaming and aggressive continuous batching, we intermittently hit GPU OOMs during peak windows. Current responses are coarse (full model fallback or global batch contraction) which hurt latency or quality. We need a fine-grained, low-latency mitigation that avoids full request drops and preserves high-priority traffic and SLOs.

Goals: Implement a surgical degradation and retry adapter that combines: (1) bandwidth-aware KV eviction lanes (cohort-based eviction tuned to token bandwidth and prefix importance), (2) a deferred-retry adapter that transparently retries a subset of requests after a short backoff with reduced KV/prefetch budget, and (3) an ordered heterogeneous fallback ladder to micro-quantized models for requests that cannot be served within memory. The system should maintain per-request correctness bounds, expose observability for cost/latency/quality tradeoffs, and integrate with rollouts/canaries.

Constraints: Must not require model graph changes; should be compatible with existing runtime kernel selection and batching pipeline; low added CPU overhead; no long blocking GC-style pauses; graceful behavior for streaming responses and tool-calls.

Proposed approach:
- KV cohort lanes: classify requests into small cohorts by recent token bandwidth (low/medium/high) and by prefix criticality (control tokens vs ephemeral). Each cohort gets a soft KV budget. Eviction within a cohort uses a recency+semantic-score heuristic so important prefixes remain while noisy long-tails are compacted.
- Bandwidth-aware admission: continuous-batcher considers cohort budgets when admitting tokens; high-bandwidth noisy requests get a smaller per-request admission window during congestion.
- Deferred-retry adapter: when admission fails due to anticipated memory pressure, requests are tagged and returned to a short retry queue (50-250ms) with a reduced KV reservation and optional prefix trimming. The adapter ownership is per-request: client sees a transparent micro-delay (streaming clients keep previous chunks) and the runtime tracks retry outcomes for telemetry.
- Micro-fidelity fallback ladder: if retries fail, the system selects from an ordered ladder of fallbacks (micro-quantized variant -> smaller context model -> local cached stub) with fidelity annotations. Switching preserves as much KV prefix as possible via snapshot deltas.
- Observability & controls: expose new console metrics (cohort eviction rate, retry latency percentiles, fallback ladder hits, request-level fidelity tag) and an operational toggle to bias for latency vs quality.

Why different from existing systems: Rather than a single global eviction or model swap, this design slices workloads into dynamic lanes and uses short deferred retries to avoid irrevocable quality drops. It balances token-level admission, KV preservation, and model fallback in a feedback loop that optimizes for SLOs rather than raw memory throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Implement KV cohort lanes and integrate with admission controller so that cohort budgets are enforced during admission
Deferred-retry adapter returns successfully for >= 85% of admissions that initially failed due to predicted memory pressure within 250ms median retry latency
Fallback ladder selection reduces hard OOMs by >= 90% in synthetic mixed-workload tests without exceeding 5% increase in P95 latency for high-priority cohort
New console metrics are emitted (cohort_eviction_rate, deferred_retry_p50/p95, fallback_hits) and dashboards created
E2E integration tests covering streaming sessions, tool-calls, and multi-tenant noise that assert no silent token loss and no user-visible corruption
decisions: Use cohort budgets (soft quotas) rather than strict per-request caps to allow opportunistic cache reuse
Deferred retry window will be adaptive between 50ms-250ms based on recent retry success rate; initial implementation hard-coded to 100ms median
Fallback ladder will be ordered by minimal quality impact: micro-quantized variant -> trimmed context on same model -> smaller model variant; final fallback to stub local responder
Maintain KV snapshot deltas for minimal prefix restoration when switching models to avoid full warmstart penalties
progress_updates: 2026-01-20: Spike finished — implemented a prototype cohort classifier and simulated eviction in the node-local runtime. Observed 2x reduction in hot-prefix evictions compared to LRU under synthetic long-prefix workloads.
2026-01-27: Integrated cohort budgets into batch admission controller; initial policy reduces admission window for high-bandwidth cohort by 30% under congestion (configurable).

2026-01-30: Built deferred-retry queue and wired telemetry; in canary runs deferred retry resolved 82% of predicted-admission-failures within 120ms. Need to tune backoff policy and ensure streaming clients handle micro-delays gracefully.

2026-02-02: Implemented fallback ladder selection and KV snapshot delta mechanism. End-to-end local test shows a 92% drop in hard OOMs but small quality regressions on 7% of requests when falling back to micro-quantized variants.
comments: Marco Liu (2026-01-22): Reviewed prototype — nice results. Action: add a small CPU budgeting guard to prevent retry queue thrashing under extreme load.

Jordan Kim (Product, 2026-01-25): Need to surface fidelity tags in Console and include user-facing label for degraded responses so product can decide UX fallback. Suggested adding a 'fidelity_reason' field to response metadata.
Priya Reddy (Design, 2026-01-28): Placeholder UX for streaming micro-delay — recommend showing a subtle 'Optimizing' spinner rather than full 'retry' message to avoid confusing end users.
Sven Müller (SRE, 2026-01-31): Questioned persistence of KV snapshot deltas across restarts — recommended persisting only metadata and reconstructing deltas on warmstart to avoid disk blowup.
